a deep learning pipeline with low level convolution sub-network followed by high level Riemmanian manifold sub-network is proposed to learn discriminative features for classification of FRPs, and that the proposed method outperforms the state of the arts in classification accuracy and robustness to data shortage.
a novel pipeline is proposed for learning the representation of fixation related potentials for single trial classification.
a novel pipeline of a convolution subnetwork and a Riemannian network is proposed to learn discriminative features for single trial classification.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of feature representation learning for the single trial classification of FRPs.
the problem of measuring the target perception ability in a visual search task using EEG based brain imaging technology.
the technical foundation for the measurement of target perceptual ability with the brain imaging technique.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this work proposes a new representation learning framework for EEG based classification of fixation related potential (FRP) signals, which is capable of learning both the first order and second order statistics in the data, and the temporal ordering information in the data.
this paper proposes a new pipeline for single trial classification with FRPs that is able to effectively capture both first order and second order statistics in the data.

the proposed approach leads to a more effective and efficient representation of FRPs in the guided visual search task and thus improves the target perceptual measurement with the FRP based EEG brain imaging technology.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we proposed a new pipeline for single trial classification for the first order and second order statistics in the EEG based FRPs.
the proposed approach is capable of learning the second order statistics of data with a deep network architecture that is robust to lack of training data.
the proposed pipeline can be used as a new tool for measuring the target perception ability of a person, which can be further used for the assessment and rehabilitation of cognitive impairment.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the proposed pipeline is able to effectively capture both first order statistics and second order statistics in the data, and thus it can potentially be extended to more general applications in the field of machine learning.
the proposed pipeline is capable of learning a deep representation of second order information in EEG signals for single trial classification.

the first order and second order information in FRPs could be jointly captured with a deep neural network, which is expected to be of general interest for EEG based brain computer interface (BCI) applications.
